findings.title: Windows paths lose the subject index used for ownership
findings.description:
The newly added ownership metadata calls `extractFileIndex()`, which splits paths only on `/`. Document discovery uses platform-native `join()`, so Windows paths yield `null` instead of their filename index. I verified this using the actual extractor: a POSIX path returned `950`; its Windows equivalent returned `null`.

`resolveFixOwner()` then selects the primary checkout rather than the indexed owner, potentially fixing the wrong copy and deferring the correct one. Use platform-aware basename extraction and add Windows-path regression coverage.

findings.title: Apply-time readiness accepts stale fix plans
findings.description:
The second readiness check verifies checkout state and target-file dirtiness, but never verifies that the dry-run inputs remain unchanged. While confirmation waits, another agent can commit changes to task completion or reorder a plan, leaving a clean checkout that passes this gate.

The code then applies stale status values or line indices and automatically commits them. The inspected checkbox writer checks only that the saved line contains a checkbox—not that it belongs to the intended subject. Recompute findings after confirmation or validate captured input revisions before applying; add a regression covering committed changes between planning and application.
